findings.title: Retry-count cleanup deletes workflow reminders of all methods
findings.body: The deleteMany query deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount greater than 1 because the second OR branch does not include method: WorkflowMethods.SMS. This can delete EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders, or any future reminder type, even though the PR only intends to stop retrying SMS reminders. Add a method filter to the retry-count branch or make method a top-level AND condition.

findings.title: Error handler can abort the whole cron batch if retry-count update fails
findings.body: In the catch block, the retry-count update is not protected. If the reminder was deleted by another process or the database update fails, this update throws and terminates the handler, preventing the remaining reminders in the batch from being processed. Use updateMany or wrap this update in its own try/catch.

findings.title: All exceptions count toward the SMS retry limit
findings.body: The catch block increments retryCount for any exception thrown while preparing the SMS, including transient database errors, metadata validation errors, or template errors. After two such errors the reminder is deleted, even if the SMS provider was never contacted or the failure is transient. Consider counting only SMS provider failures or using a separate failure-handling path for unexpected errors.

findings.title: Retry count is updated with a stale value instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: Both failure paths set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read before the scheduling attempt. If the same reminder is processed concurrently or updated between read and write, increments can be lost. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation instead.

findings.title: Reminders with no message or destination are retried forever
findings.body: When message is empty or sendTo is falsy, the code skips scheduling and does not increment retryCount. Such reminders remain unscheduled and are re-fetched on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, which defeats the retry-limit behavior for permanently unsendable reminders. Consider incrementing retryCount, marking them cancelled, or deleting them after a failure threshold.
